query: Describe municipal/local government in Mexico: the generic name of local units and how many exist, the governing council and its offices (for example municipal president/mayor, trustees, councillors) with how each office is filled and its term length. Then list the current heads of the 10 most populous municipalities as of 2026-11-14: municipality name, the first-level division it belongs to, head title in English and local language, how the head is selected, and the current officeholder (full name, party, term start/end) with source URLs. Exclude sub-units of the national capital if the capital is governed differently.

offices.selection_details: Elected with the municipal slate by popular vote; indigenous customary-system municipalities choose authorities under their own community rules. A substitute can assume office on leave of the elected president. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

Elected on municipal slates, with some states providing a proportional-representation trustee; indigenous customary-system selection also exists. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

Seats filled by election on winning slates and proportional representation under state rules, or by indigenous community electoral procedures. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

text: As of 14 November 2026, Mexico has 2,462 municipalities, excluding Mexico City’s 16 differently governed boroughs. The ten listed are the largest municipalities by the 2020 census. Municipal councils comprise a president, trustees and councillors; usual three-year terms vary under state and indigenous community rules. Juárez is headed by substitute president Héctor Rafael Ortiz Orpinel following the elected president’s leave in June 2026; his personal party affiliation is unconfirmed.
